access.edition_or_version: Self-published 1936 (undelivered); widely reprinted; public domain in India

mechanics.premise: An undelivered anti-caste address that argues social reform cannot wait on gradual moral persuasion and must confront the structure of caste directly.
mechanics.tone_function: Reformist urgency fused with argument: the text presses for immediate structural change while reasoning in public about means and ends.
mechanics.time_handling: Refuses the gradualism of 'reform in good time'; frames delay as complicity.
mechanics.syntax_and_rhythm: Argumentative paragraphs with pointed, epigrammatic closings; rhetorical questions that force the reader to take a position.
mechanics.lexical_fields: Reform, urgency, reason, rights, annihilation; institutional and legal vocabulary.
mechanics.rhetorical_situation: The withdrawal of the invitation to speak becomes part of the text's own argument that the reform is being deferred; the document's publication history enacts its urgency.
mechanics.efficacy_pairing: Demands are tied to concrete proposals (political and social action), not to atmosphere alone.
mechanics.verification_note: Author, 1936 undelivered-speech status and self-publication verified via reference summary. No passage reproduced.
